covers.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve, compositing. Edit the FIRST image: the landscape quiz-show cover. Images 2, 3, 4 are strict character identity references, each showing two views of ONE existing game character. Replace only the cast and match their rendering to these game models. Left contestant: Girl from image 2, blonde ponytail, dark skateboard T-shirt, denim shorts, wristbands and cheek plaster. Right contestant: Karlan from image 3, short brown hair, grey hoodie and grey joggers, white sneakers, distinctive large oval head, heavy upper eyelids, visible eye whites and unimpressed expression. Host behind the central podium: Boss from image 4, stocky build, charcoal zip jacket over white shirt, gold chain, cropped side-part hair, cheek plaster, forearm tattoos and knowing smirk. Preserve their actual face shapes, eye construction, hair silhouettes, stocky body proportions, skin tones, outfits and recognizable details; pose them naturally as competing players and a confident presenter. These are the game's own slightly rough mischievous cartoon adults, NOT new cute toy children, NOT black-dot eyes. Preserve the original camera, two podiums and buttons, stage layout, giant star, warm/cool stage lighting, material colours and 16:9 framing. Replace the tiny generic audience faces with soft out-of-focus silhouettes consistent with this cast. Integrate lighting and contact shadows, keep the characters in the same left/right/central positions. No title, words, logo, watermark or interface. Output one finished cover, not a character sheet.
